findings.evidence: GrowthBound.lean:96 `theorem ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound ... : S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound 0 1`; Identity.lean:146 id_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup gives the toStronglyContinuousSemigroup = id X rewrite.
findings.fix: Derive it from the contraction structure: (ContractionSemigroup.id X).hasGrowthBound rewritten via id_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup (reorder so ContractionSemigroup.id precedes this lemma).
findings.issue: id_hasGrowthBound re-proves HasGrowthBound 0 1 from norm_id_le, but the PR also builds ContractionSemigroup.id, and ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound (GrowthBound.lean:96) already yields HasGrowthBound 0 1 for any contraction semigroup.

findings.evidence: Identity.lean:110-116 body is `id_generator_apply ⟨x, hx⟩`, identical statement to id_generator_apply at line 94 up to subtype packing.
findings.fix: Drop id_generator_apply_of_mem; callers can apply id_generator_apply to ⟨x, hx⟩ directly.
findings.issue: id_generator_apply_of_mem is a thin parallel restatement of id_generator_apply, differing only in whether the domain membership is passed bundled or unbundled; its proof is `id_generator_apply ⟨x, hx⟩`.

summary: New identity-semigroup material is genuinely new, but two items duplicate existing/in-PR API: the growth bound re-derives ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound, and id_generator_apply_of_mem restates id_generator_apply up to subtype defeq.
